ActionKey.description: The key of one planned action, three words; sent back unchanged to start_sync.

ByQuality.description: A count for each quality class.

fake.description: Songs that claim to be lossless and are not.

good_lossy.description: Songs that are lossy but good.

weak.description: Songs whose cutoff is 17 kHz or less.

Empty.description: An answer or a job result with nothing in it (`{}`).

EmptyKind.description: Why a page has nothing to show (a first-run or empty state), or null when it has something.

ErrorKind.description: What kind of error a report line holds (errors: network, qobuz or other; a song nobody has: not_found).

Fail.description: A problem answer: `{ok: false, kind, message}` and, from the bridge decorator, the command line's view of it (issue 39, `discjockey/hub/outcomes.py`); the window ignores the latter. `outcome`, `reason`, `next`, `person_steps` and `data` are always present on an answer of the engine, optional here so the fake bridge needs no change. `kind` can also be `bad_args` for arguments only the command line sends (contract, Problem kinds).

data.description: Facts that belong to the reason, a different object per reason (`outcomes.REASONS`); null or absent when there are none.

kind.description: Why it failed; the window reads this.

outcome.description: The command line's outcome of the problem.

person_steps.description: The steps only a person can do.

reason.description: The closed reason of the problem (`outcomes.REASONS`).

service.description: Set when a playlist service caused the problem (a SourceError); absent for every other.

setting.description: Only with kind `setting_off` (add_playlist for a link that needs a Settings choice that is off).

FailNext.description: One command that moves on after a problem.

FailOutcome.description: The command line's outcome of a problem (`outcomes.KIND_OUTCOME`).

FailPersonStep.description: One step only a person can do.

say.description: What the person does, in words.

then.description: The command that goes on afterwards, or null.

Freshness.description: How fresh the answers are, from the stored records alone: never a scan or a fetch.

read_at.description: When the playlists were last read, an ISO time; null when none was.

scanned_at.description: When the index was last scanned (a watched folder's last scan), an ISO time; null while there is no music folder, no library.db or nothing was scanned.

LibrarySort.description: The Library's order: a column name, `-` in front for descending. `order` is a playlist's own order (its read record's); the engine's default there, and `artist` elsewhere.

PlaylistLine.description: One line of playlists.txt as the window edits it.

enabled.description: Whether the line is switched on; a switched-off line is left out of the sync.

folder.description: The playlist's folder name in the library.

PlaylistService.description: A playlist service (`sources.py`): the one a playlist row, a link or a problem belongs to.

ProblemKind.description: Why an answer is not ok. The window reads `kind` and shows `message`; the command line maps each kind to an outcome (`outcomes.KIND_OUTCOME`). The command line's own `bad_args` is sent only to it.

Quality.description: A song's colour class: lossless green, good_lossy yellow, weak red (cutoff 17 kHz or less), fake purple, missing red.

Result.description: One report line (also `ActionFinished.result`, run sections and op results): the payload copy of `events.Result`.

cover_url.description: `run(run_id)` only: the cover of rows shown one by one.

cutoff_hz.description: The measured cutoff in Hz, or null.

error_kind.description: For an error line: what kind; null elsewhere.

found_status.description: upgrade_ready: the found file's status (`status` stays the current file's; a SoundCloud original can be lossless). Missing in runs saved before it.

section.description: The report section the line belongs to (`report.SECTIONS`).

source.description: Where the file came from: one of `Source`'s values, or another word the engine reports; null when there is none.

status.description: What the sound check made of the file, or null.

SettingKey.description: A choice in Settings that a read needs (its key in settings.json): `setting_off` names it in `setting`.

Source.description: Where a file came from; `manual` is a file the user bought or owns.

SourceHow.description: How a download's source was found (the engine's `source_how`): the exact Qobuz track, its ISRC, a name search, the playlist's own upload, the fallback search, or picked by the user.

Status.description: What the sound check made of a file.

TrackRow.description: One song as a list shows it: a Library row, a to-do item, a change move (to-do items add `group` and `detail`, moves add `from`, `to`, `to_not_lossless`).

added.description: The playlist day (an ISO time); for an own file the day Discjockey first saw it.

cover_url.description: The media URL of the embedded cover, else the Spotify image URL, else null (show a placeholder).

cutoff_hz.description: The measured cutoff in Hz, if measured; `quality_label` is its words.

folder.description: The playlist folder the file is in; empty for the user's own songs from the import, which belong to no playlist folder.

hidden.description: Whether the user hid the song.

in_playlists.description: Whether a playlist still holds the song.

own.description: A file of the user's own that the import found (no playlist holds it): the table never dims it. False for a downloaded or bought one.

path.description: The file's path (absolute for the user's own songs), or null when there is none.

quality.description: The colour class: lossless green, good_lossy yellow, weak red, fake purple, missing red.

quality_label.description: The words next to the colour: LOSSLESS, 20.0 kHz, LOSSY, FAKE · 16.0 kHz, NOT FOUND.

source.description: Where the file came from, or null.

source_name.description: The source in short words: Qobuz, YT Music, SoundCloud, YouTube, bought; `own file` for a file the import found.

status.description: What the sound check made of the file.

upgrade_ready.description: Whether a better version is waiting.

Which.description: Which file of a song: the one in the library now, or the parked better version.
